content.title: Utilities Transparency
content.summary: Arvada's city government is focused on maintaining and upgrading its water, sewer, and stormwater infrastructure, much of which dates back to the mid-20th century. Long-range plans were developed to prioritize necessary improvements by 2023, ensuring reliable service for residents. Funding for these projects comes from customer rates, service fees, and system development charges from new developments, with annual adjustments approved by the City Council.
content.body:
## Current Projects

City-owned construction related to water, sewer, stormwater, and transportation projects are linked on a map on the [Public Improvement Projects webpage](/612). Many of these projects also have individual project pages on the [Current Projects page](/843).

## Background

Arvada relies on reliable water, sewer and stormwater services. From the water in your glass to the suds down the drain and the rain you watch drip off roofs, these services keep our community safe and healthy.

These systems depend on critical infrastructure—whether that be to treat your water, carry it through the sewer system, or guide rainwater safely back to our waterways. Many components of these systems were built decades ago as Arvada grew through the 60s to 80s. As systems age and reach the end of useful life, we need to reinvest in them to ensure they can provide Arvada with the same high-quality service in the future.

### Long-range planning

In Fall 2020, City Council provided strategic direction to complete long-range plans for water, wastewater and storm infrastructure by 2023. These plans provide staff with a roadmap to prioritize work that needs to be done in our systems. The City team completed the plans in 2021 and 2022, and the results are being used to prioritize work for immediate, short-term and longer-term needs.

### About our systems

Arvada residents rely on their water, sewer and storm systems to be there when they need them. That infrastructure requires regular maintenance and, at times, major investments in order to keep the system functioning 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days per year.

- The City's water and sewer systems date to the early 20th century with current components installed starting in the 1950s.
- Between the 1960s and 1980s, Arvada residents provided a funding boost to our water and sewer systems. Those infrastructure components are reaching the end of their useful life.
- The City's water and sewer systems are vast, with raw water components, two drinking water treatment facilities, over 600 miles of water pipe, and over 450 miles of wastewater pipe.

## Funding sources

Each year, the City team prioritizes projects in our system to keep delivering the level of service residents have come to expect. Some work builds capacity for new users and some work maintains, replaces and rehabilitates the existing system.

- Maintaining, replacing and rehabilitating our vast water and wastewater systems is paid for through [customer rates and service fees](/460).
- [System development charges (SDCs)](/1156) are collected from new homes and businesses to pay for the new capacity needed to serve them. Once in the City system, these customers pay rates and service fees like everyone else.

City Council approves annual adjustments to customer paid water, wastewater, and stormwater rates and fees and developer-paid System Development Charges (SDCs), sometimes called "tap fees." More information about this process can be found in the presentations to Council below.

For reference, the 10-year financials for the water, wastewater, and stormwater enterprise funds can be viewed in the [City's Budget Book (PDF)](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=6866c32c7ce3b).

## Learn more

Listen to the Inside Arvada podcast episode about funding water, wastewater, and stormwater services using the player below or wherever you listen to podcasts, including [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/16782583-inside-arvada-s-pavement-program-with-ben-sawaya)(with transcript).
